title: China warns US of countermeasures over new AI chip remote access curbs
excerpt: China's commerce ministry vowed countermeasures if the US enforces new curbs on remote access to AI chips, days before a Xi-Trump summit.
content_html:
China said on Tuesday it would hit back if the US goes ahead with new limits on its access to advanced AI chips. Its commerce ministry said it strongly opposes the rules, Bloomberg reported.

The ministry also asked Washington to settle the dispute through talks, Reuters reported. TNW has not seen the ministry’s original statement.

“If the US persists, China will take countermeasures to firmly safeguard its sovereignty, security and development interests,” the ministry said.

The US Commerce Department issued the rules on Monday. They aim to stop Chinese firms from renting Nvidia chips in data centres abroad. They also require a licence to ship top chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, according to Free Malaysia Today.

Until now, Chinese firms could legally rent Nvidia’s best chips by the hour in countries such as Thailand and Malaysia. In May, Washington had moved to close a related loophole covering Chinese firms’ overseas units.

The ministry said the new curbs go against deals struck by the two leaders. It also said they put global chip supply at risk, Bloomberg reported.

The dispute comes days before Xi Jinping hosts Donald Trump at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. A trade truce that cut tariffs last year is due to end in January, according to Bloomberg.

Calls for tighter curbs grew after Nvidia boss Jensen Huang quit last week. Huang, the best-known critic of chip controls in the industry, had admitted an affair with Alice Huang. US officials suspect she is a Chinese spy.
